Tutorial Steps

Step 1

You will start to build Roasted Duck Delivery simulation project. This form will contain a delivery grid, monitor delivery status, oven and vehicle controls. Start a new project in Visual C#. Once created, it is recommended that you immediately save it with the name you choose. That way, folders and file structures will be created.

 

Just like the previous projects, the form used on this project is quite large. Place a panel control on the left side of the form. The panel is a square with dimensions of 500 x 500 pixels. On the right side, add 2 group boxes at the top (each with a label control) and a picture box below the two group boxes. Place a list box control and a label control in the picture box. Place the other group box under the picture box control. In this group box, place 8 square picture control boxes (to display grilled fish) and two button controls.

 

Figure 3.5 All controls used and their sizes and positions on the form

 

Then, add two more group boxes and two button controls. Add labels to the two group boxes and to the second group box, add a button control. For all label controls, set the AutoSize property to False so resizing can be done and set (temporarily) the BorderStyle property to FixedSingle so you can see the edges of the label. Add two small picture box controls under the two button controls (this cannot be seen when the project is run). Finally, add four timer controls to the form. These four timer controls will be in the area below the form, as shown in Figure 3.5.

 

The control panel contains the delivery grid. The first two group boxes with labels display time and sales. The picture box control (with list and label boxes) displays order and scooter status. The third group box (with picture boxes and two buttons) displays and controls the roasting of ducks in the oven. The fourth group box displays the number of ducks that were roasted. The last group box is used to load roasted duck into the scooter. The last buttons (one to start and pause the game and one more button to stop and exit the project). Timer controls are used to control hour, order time, oven, and scooter.

This completes the form design. However, you still need a grid on the form. This grid itself will use more than 400 label controls added to the Load event procedure on the form. To do this, you need to know how to add controls when the program starts and how to link those controls to event procedures.

 

Step 3

When building a Visual C# application, the process of adding controls and setting properties when designing is quite easy and simple. Sometimes, it is more beneficial to add controls when the program runs. For example, in this project, you need a 21 x 21 grid consisting of label controls. With short code, you can automate the work of adding controls to the form when the program runs. You also delete it if you like.

 

To add a control when the program runs, you need five steps: (1) declare a control, (2) create a control, (3) set control properties, (4) add a control to the form, and (5) link the event procedure. You will see each of these steps separately for a generic control named MyControl with the type of ControlType .

 

The first step is to declare a control using the usual statement. You can also declare array that contain controls. Then, the control is created using a constructor: MyControl = new ControlType() .

 

At this point, MyControl is set with default properties. You can change the value of each property as you wish. Specifically, you need to set values ​​for the Left and Top properties. Otherwise, all of your new controls will overlap in the upper left corner of the form ( Left = 0, Right = 0 ). You can also change the Width and Height properties. After the properties are set, the control can be added to the form using the Add method of the Controls object: this.Controls.Add(MyControl) .

 

In this project, define a two-dimensional form-level array that contains the following label controls:

 

1

Label[,] DeliveryGrid = new Label[21, 21];

 

You will use the 0-th elements of the DeliveryGrid to represent column and row labels. You will ignore the DeliveryGrid (0, 0) , the grid in the upper left corner.

 

The code to create this grid and display it in the control panel ( pnlGrid ) is placed in the Load event procedure of the form:

private void FormDuckDelivery_Load( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    int w = pnlGrid.Width / 22;

    int l = w;

    int t = w;

 

    // j is row, i is column; Creates one row at a time

    for ( int j = 0; j < 21; j++)

    {

        for ( int i = 0; i < 21; i++)

        {

            DeliveryGrid[i, j] = new Label();

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Width = w;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Height = w;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Top = t;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Left = l;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Font =

                new Font( "Microsoft Sans Serif" , 10,

                FontStyle.Bold);

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].TextAlign =

                ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter;

 

            if (i == 0)

            {

                if (j != 0)

                {

                    // Row number

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text = j.ToString();

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Width =

                        Convert.ToInt32(1.5 * w);

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Left =

                        Convert.ToInt32(0.5 * w);

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.DarkBlue;

                }

            }

            else if (j == 0)

            {

                if (i != 0)

                {

                    // Column letter

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text =

                        (( char ) (i + 64)).ToString();

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.DarkBlue;

                }

            }

            else

            {

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].BorderStyle =

                    BorderStyle.FixedSingle;

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].BackColor = Color.White;

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.Yellow;

 

                if (i < 10)

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag = "0" + i.ToString();

                else

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag = i.ToString();

                if (j < 10)

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag += "0" + j.ToString();

                else

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag += j.ToString();

 

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].Click +=

                    new System. EventHandler( this . DeliveryGrid _Click);

            }

            pnlGrid.Controls.Add(DeliveryGrid[i, j]);

            l += w;

        }

 

        // New row

        l = w;

        t += w;

    }

}

 

This code builds a label control grid, one row at a time. Each control is declared first, and then the Top , Left , Width , and Height properties are given a value. You will use a square-sized label control, based on the width of the panel (1/23 of the width of the panel, so that there is still space left). You start from the top left corner, then to the right. After a row has been created, the Top property is incremented down one row and the Left property is returned to the left edge. Other properties are given based on location. Controls with column labels (J = 0) and row labels (I = 0) do not have the edge and are given letters or numbers accordingly. Notice how the row labels are shifted slightly to the left to make two-digit space. Internal labels (I = 1 to 20, J = 1 to 20) have a BorderStyle edge and a lime background to give a grid effect.

You are now starting to add other elements to this game, one by one. Step 6

The first element added to this game is time. The time will start at 6.00 and stop at 11:00. You certainly don't want the game to end completely in five hours, so you need to speed things up a bit. You need to decide how fast you need and still be able to play the game. This requires adjusting parameters.

 

 

Figure 3.7 grpOven and grpScooter initially disabled

 

The time will be controlled by the timer control with the name timTime . With each Tick event for this control, you will add one minute to the time. You will define a constant ( MSecPerMen ) that tells you how many milliseconds ( Interval property of timTime ) needed for each minute of the hour. You can choose 15 minutes to complete a game, or simulate 300 minutes (5 hours x 60 minutes / hour) of delivering ducks. So, you need to call the Tick event 300 times in 900000 milliseconds (15 minutes x 60 seconds / minutes x 1000 milliseconds / second). The constant to be used is MSecPerMen = 900000/300 = 3000 milliseconds / minute. Add this constant to the form-level declaration:

 

1

const int MSecPerMen = 3000;

 

And, add this one line of code at the end of the Load event procedure of the form to create a timer control:

 

1

timTime.Interval = MSecPerMen

 

As mentioned, with each Tick event, you add one minute to displayed time. Add the following to the form-level declaration:

 

1

int HourTime, MinuteTime;

 

The Tick event procedure of the timTime control is given as follows:

private void timTime_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    MinuteTime++;

    if (MinuteTime > 59)

    {

        MinuteTime = 0;

        HourTime++;

        if (HourTime == 11)

        {

            lblTime.Text = "11:00" ;

            btnExitStop.PerformClick();

            return ;

        }

    }

    lblTime.Text = HourTime.ToString() + ":" ;

    if (MinuteTime < 10)

        lblTime.Text += "0" ; lblTime.Text += MinuteTime.ToString();

}

 

Notice that after 11:00 is reached, the game stops by clicking ExitStop button.

 

Step 7

Now, you will write code that starts, pauses, starts, and stops the time in this game. You also need to add a code to exit the game. Two button controls control the game, btnStartPause and btnExitStop . These two buttons have certain interactions. The btnStartPause control has three possible Text properties.

 

If the Text property is Start Game when clicked, the game will be initialized and will be in play mode:

  • Change Text property to Pause Game .
  • Initialize the time to 6:00.
  • Start timTime .
  • Change Text property of btnExitStop to Stop Game .

 

If the Text property is Pause Game when clicked, the game will enter in pause mode:

  • Change the Text property to Start Again .
  • Stop the timTime .
  • Disable btnExitStop .

 

If the Text property is Start Again when clicked, the game will enter play mode:

  • Change the Text property to Pause Game .
  • Start timTime .
  • Enable btnExitStop .

 

The code that summarizes the steps above is placed in the Click event procedure of btnStartPause :

private void btnStartPause_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (btnStartPause.Text == "Start Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Text = "Stop  Game" ;

 

        HourTime = 6;

        MinuteTime = 0;

        lblTime.Text = "6:00" ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    else if (btnStartPause.Text == "Pause Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Start Again" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = false ;

        timTime.Enabled = false ;

        grpOven.Enabled = false ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

    }

    else

    {

        // Game starts again

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = true ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    }

}

 

Pay attention to the pause mode and play mode, you also disable/enable grpOven and grpScooter as needed.

Step 12

In this project, orders are randomly telephoned. Orders (time, location, and number of ducks) are displayed in the list box control. Number of roasted ducks ordered are displayed at the right location on the delivery grid. You then use this information to send the scooter to deliver the roasted duck.

 

Here are the rules made for ordering (you can change it if you like):

  • Orders arrive at random times, within 1 to 7 minutes of increment.
  • Orders originate from random locations on the delivery grid.
  • Each order is 1 to 5 roasted ducks, using this probability: 1 roasted duck, 30 percent; 2 roasted ducks, 20 percent; 3 roasted ducks, 20 percent; 4 roasted ducks, 15 percent; 5 roasted ducks, 15 percent.
  • No orders can be received after 10:30 so the scooter can complete the order.

 

As mentioned, order information will be displayed in the list box control. You use a specific format for it. For example, say the order arrived at 6:20, from the G12 grid location, for 2 roasted ducks. The information on the list box is 6:20 G 12 -> 2.

 

Two arrays will be used to track order information. DuckArr is a two-dimensional array that says how many ducks are ordered at a grid location and TimeDuckArr is a two-dimensional array that contains the ordering time (in minutes). Add the following two declarations at the form-level:

 

1

2

int [,] DuckArr = new int [21, 21];

int [,] TimeDuckArr = new int [21, 21];

 

timPhone timer will control how often orders arrive. The Interval property will be set randomly. Add a declaration that creates this random object in the form-level declaration:

        HourTime = 6;

        MinuteTime = 0;

        timPhone.Interval = MSecPerMen * (1 + MyRandom.Next(7));

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    else if (btnStartPause.Text == "Pause Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Start Again" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = false ;

        timTime.Enabled = false ;

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        grpOven.Enabled = false ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

    }

    else

    {

        // Game starts again

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = true ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

}

private void timPhone_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    int i, j, k;

    String Message;

    SoundPhone.Play();

 

    if (HourTime == 10 && MinuteTime >= 30)

    {

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        return ;

    }

 

    do {

        i = 1 + MyRandom.Next(20);

        j = 1 + MyRandom.Next(20);

    } while (DuckArr[i, j] != 0);

 

    k = MyRandom.Next(100);

 

    if (k <= 29)

        DuckArr[i, j] = 1;

    else if (k <= 49)

        DuckArr[i, j] = 2;

    else if (k <= 69)

        DuckArr[i, j] = 3;

    else if (k <= 84)

        DuckArr[i, j] = 4;

    else

        DuckArr[i, j] = 5;

 

    TimeDuckArr[i, j] = MinuteTime + 60 * HourTime;

 

    // Creates order string

    Message = lblTime.Text + " " ;

    if (lblTime.Text.Length == 4)

        Message = " " + Message;

    Message += (( char )(i + 64)).ToString() + " " ;

 

    if (j < 10)

        Message += " " ;

    Message += j.ToString() + " -> " + DuckArr[i, j].ToString();

 

    lstOrder.Items.Add(Message);

    lstOrder.Refresh();

    DeliveryGrid[i, j].BackColor = Color.DarkGreen;

    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text = DuckArr[i, j].ToString();

    timPhone.Interval = MSecPerMen * (1 + MyRandom.Next(7));

}

 

Figure 3.10 The phone starts ringing, with orders placed in the list box and the delivery grid area

 

In this code, you ring the telephone. If the time is past 10:30, this routine is no longer executed. Next, you select an unselected random column (I) and a random row (J) for the order. Using the set percentages, the number ordered roasted ducks are stored in the DuckArr . Likewise, ordering time is stored in TimeDuckArr .

 

Then, the text string that will be placed in the list box is formatted and added to the list box. The associated grid location is marked with a dark violet background and the number of ordered ducks. Before the procedure is finished executing, a new random interval value is calculated. This will give you a delay (between 1 and 7 minutes) until the next order is called.

Step 17

Once you know where the order came from, you need to roast ordered ducks in the oven. The grpOven group control box is now used. As you can see, you can roast, at most, eight pieces of duck at a time, which is shown by the picture box controls. You need other rules, and you can change them if you like. After the duck is roasted (it takes 10 minutes), the duck is placed in the grpRoast group box for storage. Up to 20 pieces of duck can be stored there. All ducks that have been roasted and not adequately placed in storage must be thrown away, which wastes money.

private void FormDuckDelivery_Load( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    int w = pnlGrid.Width / 22;

    int l = w;

    int t = w;

 

    // j is row, i is column; Creates one row at a time

    for ( int j = 0; j < 21; j++)

    {

        for ( int i = 0; i < 21; i++)

        {

            DeliveryGrid[i, j] = new Label();

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Width = w;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Height = w;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Top = t;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Left = l;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Font =

                new Font( "Microsoft Sans Serif" , 10,

                FontStyle.Bold);

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].TextAlign =

                ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter;

 

            if (i == 0)

            {

                if (j != 0)

                {

                    // Row number

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text = j.ToString();

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Width =

                        Convert.ToInt32(1.5 * w);

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Left =

                        Convert.ToInt32(0.5 * w);

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.DarkBlue;

                }

            }

            else if (j == 0)

            {

                if (i != 0)

                {

                    // Column letter

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text =

                        (( char ) (i + 64)).ToString();

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.DarkBlue;

                }

            }

            else

            {

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].BorderStyle =

                    BorderStyle.FixedSingle;

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].BackColor = Color.White;

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.Yellow;

 

                if (i < 10)

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag = "0" + i.ToString();

                else

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag = i.ToString();

                if (j < 10)

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag += "0" + j.ToString();

                else

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag += j.ToString();

            }

            pnlGrid.Controls.Add(DeliveryGrid[i, j]);

            l += w;

        }

 

        // New row

        l = w;

        t += w;

    }

    DuckInOven[0] = picDuck1;

    DuckInOven[1] = picDuck2;

    DuckInOven[2] = picDuck3;

    DuckInOven[3] = picDuck4;

    DuckInOven[4] = picDuck5;

    DuckInOven[5] = picDuck6;

    DuckInOven[6] = picDuck7;

    DuckInOven[7] = picDuck8;

    grpOven.Enabled = false ;

    grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

    timTime.Interval = MSecPerMen;

    timOven.Interval = MSecPerMen;

 

    SoundGameOver =

        new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath +

        "\\gameover.wav" );

    SoundPhone =

        new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath +

        "\\phone.wav" );

}

private void btnStartPause_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (btnStartPause.Text == "Start Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Text = "Stop  Game" ;

 

        // Clears grid

        for ( int i = 1; i < 21; i++)

        {

            for ( int j = 1; j < 21; j++)

            {

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].BackColor = Color.White;

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text = "" ;

                DuckArr[i, j] = 0;

                TimeDuckArr[i, j] = 0;

            }

        }

        lstOrder.Items.Clear();

 

        for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++)

            DuckInOven[i].Visible = false ;

        DuckRoast = 0;

        DuckReady = MaxDuckRoast;

        TotalDuckRoast = DuckReady;

        lblDuckReady.Text = DuckReady.ToString();

 

        HourTime = 6;

        MinuteTime = 0;

        lblTime.Text = "6:00" ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        timPhone.Interval = MSecPerMen * (1 + MyRandom.Next(7));

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    else if (btnStartPause.Text == "Pause Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Start Again" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = false ;

        timTime.Enabled = false ;

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        OvenOn = timOven.Enabled;

        grpOven.Enabled = false ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

    }

    else

    {

        // Game starts again

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = true ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        timOven.Enabled = OvenOn;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    }

}

private void btnRoastDuck_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    int hOut, mOut;

    if (DuckRoast == 0)

        return ;

 

    grpOven.BackColor = Color.Red;

    btnPutIntoOven.Enabled = false ;

    btnRoastDuck.Enabled = false ;

    hOut = HourTime;

    mOut = MinuteTime + RoastTime;

 

    if (mOut > 59)

    {

        mOut -= 60;

        hOut++;

    }

 

    if (DuckRoast == 1)

        grpOven.Text = "Ducks finished roasting on " ;

    else

        grpOven.Text = "Ducks finished roasting on " ;

    grpOven.Text += hOut.ToString() + ":" ;

 

    if (mOut < 10)

        grpOven.Text += "0" ;

    grpOven.Text += mOut.ToString();

    RemMinuteRoast = RoastTime;

    timOven.Enabled = true ;

}

Step 25

With each Tick event on the oven timer ( timOven ), you need to do the following steps:

  • If RemMinuteRoast <> 0 , RemMinuteRoast is decreased by one; if not, proceed to the next step.

  • Turn off the oven.
  • Increase both DuckReady and TotalDuckRoast by 1, check the limit of MaxDuckReady .
  • Set the Text property of grpOven to Oven Off ; change the background color to deep pink.
  • Remove all duck picture boxes.
  • Set DuckRoast to 0.
  • Enable btnPutIntoOvenbutton and btnRoastDuck buttons.

private void timOven_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (RemMinuteRoast != 0)

        RemMinuteRoast--;

    else

    {

        SoundDing.Play();

        timOven.Enabled = false ;

        DuckReady += DuckRoast;

        TotalDuckRoast += DuckRoast;

 

        if (DuckReady > MaxDuckReady)

            DuckReady = MaxDuckReady;

        lblDuckReady.Text = DuckReady.ToString();

 

        grpOven.Text = "Oven Off" ;

        grpOven.BackColor = Color.DeepPink;

 

        for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++)

            DuckInOven[i].Visible = false ;

        DuckRoast = 0;

        btnPutIntoOven.Enabled = true ;

        btnRoastDuck.Enabled = true ;

    }

}

private void btnLoadScooter_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (DuckReady == 0)

        return ;

    if (DuckReady > MaxDuckInScooter)

    {

        DuckInScooter += MaxDuckInScooter;

    lblInScooter.Text = DuckInScooter.ToString();

    btnLoadScooter.Enabled = false ;

}

Step 32

After the roasted ducks are loaded into the delivery scooter, you are ready to make the delivery. Click on a location on the delivery grid and the scooter will travel from the restaurant to that location. You follow the same process so that the scooter returns to the restaurant when you need more roasted ducks. There is a lot to be done here: defining the location of the restaurant (randomly); detect clicks on the delivery grid; identify which label controls are clicked; and move the delivery scooter to the location that was clicked.

 

You need a number of variables to track a scooter. Add the following declarations at the form-level:

DuckC and DuckR are column and row numbers for duck restaurant location on the delivery grid (marked with the X symbol). DeliveryC and DeliveryR are column and row numbers for delivery (label control that is clicked). ScooterC and ScooterR are the column and row numbers for the current scooter location. DeltaC and DeltaR are the difference between the position of the scooter and the delivery. Finally, Distance is the number of grid locations that need to be traveled by scooter and ScooterMove indicates whether the scooter is now moving (used for pause mode in the game).

1

const int MinPer20Square = 3;

 

This tells how many minutes it will take to move the scooter across the delivery grid (20 square squares per minute).

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Top = t;

private void btnStartPause_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (btnStartPause.Text == "Start Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Text = "Stop  Game" ;

 

        // Clears grid

        for ( int i = 1; i < 21; i++)

        {

            for ( int j = 1; j < 21; j++)

            {

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].BackColor = Color.White;

                DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text = "" ;

                DuckArr[i, j] = 0;

                TimeDuckArr[i, j] = 0;

            }

        }

        lstOrder.Items.Clear();

 

        for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++)

            DuckInOven[i].Visible = false ;

        DuckRoast = 0;

        DuckReady = MaxDuckRoast;

        TotalDuckRoast = DuckReady;

        lblDuckReady.Text = DuckReady.ToString();

 

        DuckInScooter = 0;

        lblInScooter.Text = "0" ;

        btnLoadScooter.Enabled = true ;

 

        // Initialize destination and scooter location

        DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = null ;

        DuckC = 2 + MyRandom.Next(18);

        DuckR = 2 + MyRandom.Next(18);

        DeliveryGrid[DuckC, DuckR].BackColor = Color.Black;

        DeliveryGrid[DuckC, DuckR].Text = "X" ;

        ScooterC = DuckC;

        ScooterR = DuckR;

        Distance = 0;

        lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in:\r\n" +

            Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

 

        HourTime = 6;

        MinuteTime = 0;

        lblTime.Text = "6:00" ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        timPhone.Interval = MSecPerMen * (1 + MyRandom.Next(7));

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    else if (btnStartPause.Text == "Pause Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Start Again" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = false ;

        timTime.Enabled = false ;

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        OvenOn = timOven.Enabled;

        grpOven.Enabled = false ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

    }

    else

    {

        // Game starts again

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = true ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        timOven.Enabled = OvenOn;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    }

}

 

You first remove all previous scooters on the delivery grid. Then, the roasted duck restaurant is placed on a random grid and marked with the symbol X. The scooter is positioned at this location and Distance is initialized zero. Message is used to announce that the scooter is currently in the restaurant. Notice how you use the ScooterMove variable to pause and restart the game.

private void DeliveryGrid_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (!timScooter.Enabled && grpScooter.Enabled &&

        !btnLoadScooter.Enabled)

    {

        DeliveryR =

        deltaC = DeliveryC - ScooterC;

        deltaR = DeliveryR - ScooterR;

        timScooter.Enabled = true ;

    }

Step 40

Now, you will make the scooter move to the selected location. Remember the two small picture boxes hidden behind the Start Game button ( picHScooter and picVScooter )? You will use it to show how the scooter moves on the delivery grid.

 

By clicking on a grid location, timScooter will be enabled. With each Tick event at this timer, you move the scooter by a square box. You make horizontal movement first, then vertical movement. The steps required are as follows:

  • Remove the image of the scooter in its current position.
  • If DeltaC <> 0 : Increase Distance by 1; Set the image to picHScooter.Image ; Recalculate ScooterC ; Recalculate DeltaC .
  • If DeltaR <> 0 : Increase Distance by 1; Set the image to picVScooter.Image ; Recalculate ScooterR ; Recalculate DeltaR .
  • Draw a scooter at a new location.
  • If ScooterC = DeliveryC and ScooterR = DeliveryR :
  • Play certain sound;
  • Disable timScooter ;
  • If ScooterC = DuckC and ScooterR = DuckR : return to the duck restaurant; set message; remove the image of the scooter; set DuckInScooter to 0; Enable btnLoadScooter .
  • If it's not in the restaurant, the scooter is in the location that was clicked: display a message; check delivery status.

 

Figure 3.16 The location clicked in delivery grid is E 13

 

This process seems to require many steps, but is actually quite simple. Note, especially, when you re-enable btnLoadScooter when the delivery scooter returns to the duck restaurant to reload the ducks into the scooter.

private void timScooter_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    Image ScooterImage;

    DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = null ;

 

    // Moves horizontally first

    if (deltaC != 0)

    {

        Distance++;

        ScooterImage = picHScooter.Image;

        ScooterC += Math.Sign(deltaC);

        deltaC = DeliveryC - ScooterC;

    }

    else

    {

        Distance++;

        ScooterImage = picHScooter.Image;

        ScooterR += Math.Sign(deltaR);

        deltaR = DeliveryR - ScooterR;

    }

 

    DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = ScooterImage;

 

    if (ScooterC == DeliveryC && ScooterR == DeliveryR)

    {

        SoundScooter.Play();

        timScooter.Enabled = false ;

 

        if (ScooterC == DuckC && ScooterR == DuckR)

        {

            lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in Restaurant :\r\n" +

                Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

            DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = null ;

            DuckInScooter = 0;

            lblInScooter.Text = "0" ;

            btnLoadScooter.Enabled = true ;

        }

 

        else

        {

            lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in " +

                Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

 

            // Checks delivery status

        }

    }

}

Step 42

After the delivery scooter arrives at the chosen location, you need to check the delivery status at that location. You will also determine how delivery results in your income. The rules that are applied are as follows:

  • Timely delivery is in the range of 30 minutes. Timely delivery costs in Rp. 10,000 for each roasted duck delivered. Timely delivery will have a green background on the grid.
  • Delayed delivery is between 30 to 60 minutes. Delayed delivery costs Rp. 5,000 for each roasted duck delivered. Delayed delivery will have a red background on the grid.
  • After 60 minutes, the order will be canceled and there is a penalty of Rp. 1,000 for each roasted duck that is not delivered.
  • Rp. 3,000 is cost to roast each duck.
  • Rp. 100 is cost for each square box taken by the delivery scooter.

        timPhone.Interval = MSecPerMen * (1 + MyRandom.Next(7));

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    else if (btnStartPause.Text == "Pause Game" )

    {

        btnStartPause.Text = "Start Again" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = false ;

        timTime.Enabled = false ;

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        timPhone.Enabled = false ;

        OvenOn = timOven.Enabled;

        grpOven.Enabled = false ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

    }

    else

    {

        // Game starts again

        btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

        btnExitStop.Enabled = true ;

        timTime.Enabled = true ;

        timPhone.Enabled = true ;

        timOven.Enabled = OvenOn;

        grpOven.Enabled = true ;

        grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

    }

}

 

 

Step 44

Note that the indication of timely delivery is indicated by a white background color on the grid and late delivery is indicated by a red background color on the grid. The grid background is initialized in violet. After 30 minutes have passed after an order has been made, you need to change the background to red. And, after 60 minutes have passed for an order, it will be removed from the grid with penalty fees applied. This is all done in the Tick event procedure of timTime . At each Tick event, the following steps are performed:

  • Check whether 60 minutes have passed for the first item in the list box. This is the longest order on the list and the only candidate to be deleted. If 60 minutes have passed, DeliveryCancel will be increased by the number of roasted duck ordered and the order will be removed from the delivery grid and list box.
  • For all other items in the list box, you check whether 30 minutes have passed. If so, and the background of the order location grid is not red, the background color is changed to red.

 

Modify the Tick event of timTime to implement the steps above:

private void timTime_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    int TotalMinuteTime;

    int c, r;

    String s;

    bool Expire = false ;

 

    MinuteTime++;

    if (MinuteTime > 59)

    {

        MinuteTime = 0;

        HourTime++;

        if (HourTime == 11)

        {

            lblTime.Text = "11:00" ;

            btnExitStop.PerformClick();

            return ;

        }

    }

    lblTime.Text = HourTime.ToString() + ":" ;

    if (MinuteTime < 10)

        lblTime.Text += "0" ; lblTime.Text += MinuteTime.ToString();

 

    // Checks delayed order - checks whether it expires

    TotalMinuteTime = MinuteTime + 60 * HourTime;

    if (lstOrder.Items.Count != 0)

    {

        for ( int i = 0; i < lstOrder.Items.Count; i++)

        {

            s = lstOrder.Items[i].ToString();

            c = (( int ) s[6]) - 64;

            r = Convert.ToInt32(s.Substring(8,2));

 

            if (i == 0 && TotalMinuteTime - TimeDuckArr[c, r] >=

                MaxOrderTime)

            {

                Expire = true ;

                DeliveryGrid[c, r].BackColor = Color.White;

                DeliveryGrid[c, r].Text = "" ;

                DeliveryCancel += DuckArr[c, r];

                DuckArr[c, r] = 0;

            }

 

            else if (TotalMinuteTime - TimeDuckArr[c, r] >=

                DelayOrderTime)

            {

                DeliveryGrid[c, r].BackColor = Color.DarkRed;

            }

        }

 

        if (Expire)

            lstOrder.Items.RemoveAt(0);

    }

}

 

Notice how you extract the column (C) and row (R) information from list box items. In the code, you use constants that are defined for timely delivery and delayed delivery.

Save and run the game. Click on the Start Game button. Notice when orders start to display a violet background, as shown in Figure 3.18. After 30 minutes, orders that have passed 30 minutes will turn red, as shown in Figure 3.19.

 

After 60 minutes, the orders are removed from the grid. Make sure the program works as desired. You can decrease MSecPerMen to speed up the timing.

 

Step 46

As seen before, after the scooter arrives at the delivery location, check on the delivery status is performed. This check is done at the Click event of the timScooter . The following steps need to be done:

  • If the delivery location does not order any duck, a message will be displayed.
  • If the delivery location requires more roasted ducks than is available, a message will be displayed.
  • If timely delivery is successful, DuckOnTime will be increased by the number of roasted ducks ordered. TotalSale is also updated.
  • If the delivery is elayed, DuckDelay will be increased by the number of roasted ducks ordered. TotalSale is also updated.
  • If delivery is successful (either on time or delayed), DuckInScooter is decremented and the order is removed from the delivery grid and from the list box control.

private void timScooter_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    Image ScooterImage;

    int i, c, r;

    String s;

    DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = null ;

 

    // Moves horizontally first

    if (deltaC != 0)

    {

        Distance++;

        ScooterImage = picHScooter.Image;

        ScooterC += Math.Sign(deltaC);

        deltaC = DeliveryC - ScooterC;

    }

    else

    {

        Distance++;

        ScooterImage = picHScooter.Image;

        ScooterR += Math.Sign(deltaR);

        deltaR = DeliveryR - ScooterR;

    }

 

    DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = ScooterImage;

 

    if (ScooterC == DeliveryC && ScooterR == DeliveryR)

    {

        SoundScooter.Play();

        timScooter.Enabled = false ;

 

        if (ScooterC == DuckC && ScooterR == DuckR)

        {

            lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in Restaurant :\r\n" +

                Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

            DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = null ;

            DuckInScooter = 0;

            lblInScooter.Text = "0" ;

            btnLoadScooter.Enabled = true ;

        }

 

        else

        {

            lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in " +

                Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

 

            // Checks delivery status

            if (DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] == 0)

            {

                lblOrder.Text += "\r\nNo Ducks Ordered" ;

            }

 

            else

            {

                if (DuckArr [DeliveryC, DeliveryR] > DuckInScooter)

                {

                    lblOrder.Text += "\r\nDucks Not Enough" ;

                }

                else

                {

                    lblOrder.Text += "\r\nDelivered " +

                        DuckArr[DeliveryC,

                        DeliveryR].ToString() + " Ducks" ;

                    if (DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] > 1)

                        lblOrder.Text += "- Thanks" ;

 

                    // check on-time or delayed delivery

                    if ((MinuteTime + 60 * HourTime) –

                        TimeDuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] <=

                        DelayOrderTime)

                    {

                        lblOrder.Text += ": On Time" ;

                        T otalSale += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] *

                            DuckSoldNet;

                        DuckOnTime += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR];

                    }

                    else

                    {

                        lblOrder.Text += ": Delayed!" ;

                        T otalSale += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] *

                            DuckDelayNet;

                        D uckDelay += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR];

                    }

 

                    lblSale.Text = "Rp. " + TotalSale.ToString();

                    D uckInScooter -= DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR];

                    lblInScooter. Text = DuckInScooter.ToString();

 

                    DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] = 0;

                    De liveryGrid[DeliveryC, DeliveryR].BackColor =

                        Color.White;

                    DeliveryGrid[DeliveryC, DeliveryR].Text = "" ;

 

                    // Removes from list

                    for (i = 0; i < lstOrder.Items.Count; i++)

                    {

                        s = lstOrder.Items[i].ToString();

                        c = (( int ) s[6]) - 64;

                        r = Convert.ToInt32(s.Substring(8,2));

                        if (c == DeliveryC && r == DeliveryR)

                            break ;

                    }

                    lstOrder.Items.RemoveAt(i);

                }

            }

        }

    }

}

 

Notice how you search the list box to find related item (matched column and row) to delete orders.

        private void FormDuckDelivery_Load( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            int w = pnlGrid.Width / 22;

            int l = w;

            int t = w;

 

            // j is row, i is column; Creates one row at a time

            for ( int j = 0; j < 21; j++)

            {

                for ( int i = 0; i < 21; i++)

                {

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j] = new Label();

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Width = w;

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Height = w;

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Top = t;

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Left = l;

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j].Font = new Font( "Microsoft Sans Serif" ,

                        10, FontStyle.Bold);

                    DeliveryGrid[i, j]. TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter;

 

                    if (i == 0)

                    {

                        if (j != 0)

                        {

                            // Row number

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text = j.ToString();

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Width = Convert.ToInt32(1.5 * w);

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Left = Convert.ToInt32(0.5 * w);

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.DarkBlue;

                        }

                    }

                    else if (j == 0)

                    {

                        if (i != 0)

                        {

                            // Column letter

                            DeliveryGrid [i, j].Text = (( char ) (i + 64)).ToString();

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.DarkBlue;

                        }

                    }

                    else

                    {

                        DeliveryGrid[i, j]. BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle;

                        DeliveryGrid[i, j].BackColor = Color.White;

                        DeliveryGrid[i, j].ForeColor = Color.Yellow;

 

                        if (i < 10)

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag = "0" + i.ToString();

                        else

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag = i.ToString();

                        if (j < 10)

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag += "0" + j.ToString();

                        else

                            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Tag += j.ToString();

 

                        DeliveryGrid[i, j].Click += new

                            System.EventHandler( this .DeliveryGrid_Click);

                    }

                    pnlGrid.Controls.Add(DeliveryGrid[i, j]);

                    l += w;

                }

 

                // New row

                l = w;

                t += w;

            }

 

            DuckInOven[0] = picDuck1;

            DuckInOven[1] = picDuck2;

            DuckInOven[3] = picDuck4;

            DuckInOven[7] = picDuck8;

            grpOven.Enabled = false ;

            grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

            timTime.Interval = MSecPerMen;

            timOven.Interval = MSecPerMen;

            timScooter.Interval = MSecPerMen * MinPer20Square / 20;

            SoundGameOver = new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath

                + "\\gameover.wav" );

            SoundPhone = new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath

                + "\\phone.wav" );

            SoundDing = new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath

                + "\\ding.wav" );

            SoundScooter = new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath

                + "\\scooter.wav" );

        }

                if (HourTime == 11)

                    lblTime.Text = "11:00" ;

                    btnExitStop.PerformClick();

                    return ;

                }

            }

 

            lblTime.Text = HourTime.ToString() + ":" ;

            if (MinuteTime < 10)

                lblTime.Text += "0" ; lblTime.Text += MinuteTime.ToString();

 

            // Checks delayed order - checks whether it expires

            TotalMinuteTime = MinuteTime + 60 * HourTime;

            if (lstOrder.Items.Count != 0)

            {

                for ( int i = 0; i < lstOrder.Items.Count; i++)

                {

                    s = lstOrder.Items[i].ToString();

                    c = (( int ) s[6]) - 64;

                    r = Convert.ToInt32(s.Substring(8,2));

 

                    if (i == 0 && TotalMinuteTime - TimeDuckArr[c, r] >= MaxOrderTime)

                    {

                        Expire = true ;

                        DeliveryGrid[c, r].BackColor = Color.White;

                        DeliveryGrid[c, r].Text = "" ;

                    else if ( TotalMinuteTime - TimeDuckArr[c, r] >= DelayOrderTime)

                    {

                        DeliveryGrid[c, r].BackColor = Color.DarkRed;

                }

 

                if (Expire)

                    lstOrder.Items.RemoveAt(0);

            }

        }

 

        private void btnStartPause_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

                DuckR = 2 + MyRandom.Next(18);

                DeliveryGrid[DuckC, DuckR].Text = "X" ;

                ScooterC = DuckC;

                ScooterR = DuckR;

                DuckOnTime = 0;

                DuckDelay = 0;

                DeliveryCancel = 0;

                TotalSale = 0;

                lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in:\r\n" + Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

 

                HourTime = 6;

                MinuteTime = 0;

                timPhone.Interval = MSecPerMen * (1 + MyRandom.Next(7));

                timPhone.Enabled = true ;

                grpOven.Enabled = true ;

                grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

            }

            else if (btnStartPause.Text == "Pause Game" )

            {

                btnStartPause.Text = "Start Again" ;

                btnExitStop.Enabled = false ;

                timTime.Enabled = false ;

                timPhone.Enabled = false ;

                OvenOn = timOven.Enabled;

                timOven.Enabled = false ;

                ScooterMove = timScooter.Enabled;

                timScooter.Enabled = false ;

                grpOven.Enabled = false ;

                grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

            }

            else

            {

                // Game starts again

                btnStartPause.Text = "Pause Game" ;

                btnExitStop.Enabled = true ;

                timTime.Enabled = true ;

                timPhone.Enabled = true ;

                timOven.Enabled = OvenOn;

                timScooter.Enabled = ScooterMove;

                grpOven.Enabled = true ;

                grpScooter.Enabled = true ;

            }

        }

 

        private void btnExitStop_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            if (btnExitStop.Text == "Stop Game" )

            {

                SoundGameOver.Play();

                btnExitStop.Text = "Exit" ;

                btnStartPause.Text = "Start Game" ;

                timTime.Enabled = false ;

                timPhone.Enabled = false ;

                timOven.Enabled = false ;

                timScooter.Enabled = false ;

 

                grpOven.Text = "Oven Off" ;

                grpOven.BackColor = Color.Blue;

                for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++)

                    DuckInOven[i].Visible = false ;

                btnPutIntoOven.Enabled = true ;

                btnRoastDuck.Enabled = true ;

 

                grpOven.Enabled = false ;

                grpScooter.Enabled = false ;

            }

            else

            {

                this .Close();

            }

        }

 

        private void timPhone_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            int i, j, k;

            String Message;

            SoundPhone.Play();

            if (HourTime == 10 && MinuteTime >= 30)

            {

                timPhone.Enabled = false ;

                return ;

            }

 

            do {

                i = 1 + MyRandom.Next(20);

                j = 1 + MyRandom.Next(20);

            } while (DuckArr[i, j] != 0);

 

            k = MyRandom.Next(100);

 

            if (k <= 29)

                DuckArr[i, j] = 1;

            else if (k <= 49)

                DuckArr[i, j] = 2;

            else if (k <= 69)

                DuckArr[i, j] = 3;

            else if (k <= 84)

                DuckArr[i, j] = 4;

            else

                DuckArr[i, j] = 5;

 

            TimeDuckArr[i, j] = MinuteTime + 60 * HourTime;

 

            // Creates order string

            Message = lblTime.Text + " " ;

            if (lblTime.Text.Length == 4)

                Message = " " + Message;

            Message += (( char )(i + 64)).ToString() + " " ;

 

            if (j < 10)

                Message += " " ;

            Message += j.ToString() + " -> " + DuckArr[i, j].ToString();

 

            lstOrder.Items.Add(Message);

            lstOrder.Refresh();

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].BackColor = Color.DarkGreen;

            DeliveryGrid[i, j].Text = DuckArr[i, j].ToString();

            timPhone.Interval = MSecPerMen * (1 + MyRandom.Next(7));

        }

 

        private void btnPutIntoOven_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            DuckRoast++;

            DuckInOven[DuckRoast - 1].Visible = true ;

            if (DuckRoast == MaxDuckRoast)

                btnPutIntoOven.Enabled = false ;

        }

 

        private void btnRoastDuck_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            int hOut, mOut;

            if (DuckRoast == 0)

                return ;

 

            grpOven.BackColor = Color.Red;

            btnPutIntoOven.Enabled = false ;

            btnRoastDuck.Enabled = false ;

            hOut = HourTime;

            mOut = MinuteTime + RoastTime;

 

            if (mOut > 59)

            {

                mOut -= 60;

                hOut++;

            }

 

            if (DuckRoast == 1)

                grpOven.Text = "Ducks finished roasting on " ;

            else

                grpOven.Text = "Ducks finished roasting on " ;

            grpOven.Text += hOut.ToString() + ":" ;

 

            if (mOut < 10)

                grpOven.Text += "0" ;

            grpOven.Text += mOut.ToString();

            RemMinuteRoast = RoastTime;

            timOven.Enabled = true ;

        }

 

        private void timOven_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            if (RemMinuteRoast != 0)

                RemMinuteRoast--;

            else

            {

                SoundDing.Play();

                timOven.Enabled = false ;

                DuckReady += DuckRoast;

                TotalDuckRoast += DuckRoast;

 

                if (DuckReady > MaxDuckReady)

                    DuckReady = MaxDuckReady;

                lblDuckReady.Text = DuckReady.ToString();

 

                grpOven.Text = "Oven Off" ;

                grpOven.BackColor = Color.DeepPink;

 

                for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++)

                    DuckInOven[i].Visible = false ;

                DuckRoast = 0;

                btnPutIntoOven.Enabled = true ;

                btnRoastDuck.Enabled = true ;

            }

        }

 

        private void btnLoadScooter_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            if (DuckReady == 0)

                return ;

            if (DuckReady > MaxDuckInScooter)

            {

                DuckInScooter += MaxDuckInScooter;

                DuckReady -= MaxDuckInScooter;

            }

            else

            {

                DuckInScooter += DuckReady;

                DuckReady = 0;

            }

 

            lblDuckReady.Text = DuckReady.ToString();

            lblInScooter.Text = DuckInScooter.ToString();

            btnLoadScooter.Enabled = false ;

        }

 

        private String Display( int c, int r)

        {

            return ((( char )(c + 64)).ToString() + " " + r.ToString());

        }

 

        private void DeliveryGrid_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            Label GridClicked;

            if (!timScooter. Enabled && grpScooter.Enabled && !btnLoadScooter.Enabled)

            {

                GridClicked = (Label)sender;

                DeliveryC =

                    Convert.ToInt32(GridClicked.Tag.ToString().Substring(0, 2));

                DeliveryR =

                    Convert.ToInt32(GridClicked.Tag.ToString().Substring(2, 2));

 

                deltaC = DeliveryC - ScooterC;

                deltaR = DeliveryR - ScooterR;

 

                if (deltaC == 0 && deltaR == 0)

                    return ;

 

                lblOrder.Text = "Scooter departs for: \r\n" + Display(DeliveryC, DeliveryR);

                timScooter.Enabled = true ;

            }

        }

 

        private void timScooter_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            Image ScooterImage;

            int i, c, r;

            String s;

 

            DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = null ;

 

            // Moves horizontally first

            if (deltaC != 0)

            {

                Distance++;

                ScooterImage = picHScooter.Image;

                ScooterC += Math.Sign(deltaC);

                deltaC = DeliveryC - ScooterC;

            }

 

            else

            {

                Distance++;

                ScooterImage = picHScooter.Image;

                ScooterR += Math.Sign(deltaR);

                deltaR = DeliveryR - ScooterR;

            }

 

            DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = ScooterImage;

 

            if (ScooterC == DeliveryC && ScooterR == DeliveryR)

            {

                SoundScooter.Play();

                timScooter.Enabled = false ;

 

                if (ScooterC == DuckC && ScooterR == DuckR)

                {

                    lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in Restaurant :\r\n" +

                        Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

                    DeliveryGrid[ScooterC, ScooterR].Image = null ;

                    DuckInScooter = 0;

                    lblInScooter.Text = "0" ;

                    btnLoadScooter.Enabled = true ;

                }

 

                else

                {

                    lblOrder.Text = "Scooter in " + Display(ScooterC, ScooterR);

 

                    // Checks delivery status

                    if (DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] == 0)

                    {

                        lblOrder.Text += "\r\nNo Ducks Ordered" ;

                    }

 

                    else

                    {

                        if (DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] > DuckInScooter)

                        {

                            lblOrder.Text += "\r\nDucks Not Enough" ;

                        }

                        else

                        {

                            lblOrder.Text += "\r\nDelivered " +

                                DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR].ToString() +

                                " Ducks" ;

                            if (DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] > 1)

                                lblOrder.Text += "- Thanks" ;

 

                            // check on-time or delayed delivery

                            if ((MinuteTime + 60 * HourTime) –

                              TimeDuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] <= DelayOrderTime)

                            {

                                lblOrder.Text += ": On Time" ;

                                TotalSale += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] * DuckSoldNet;

                                DuckOnTime += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR];

                            }

                            else

                            {

                                lblOrder.Text += ": Delayed!" ;

                                TotalSale += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] * DuckDelayNet;

                                DuckDelay += DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR];

                            }

 

                            lblSale.Text = "Rp. " + TotalSale.ToString();

                            DuckInScooter -= DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR];

                            lblInScooter.Text = DuckInScooter.ToString();

 

                            DuckArr[DeliveryC, DeliveryR] = 0;

                            DeliveryGrid[ DeliveryC, DeliveryR].BackColor = Color.White;

                            DeliveryGrid[DeliveryC, DeliveryR].Text = "" ;

 

                            // Removes from list

                            for (i = 0; i < lstOrder.Items.Count; i++)

                            {

                                s = lstOrder.Items[i].ToString();

                                c = (( int ) s[6]) - 64;

                                r = Convert.ToInt32(s.Substring(8,2));

                                if (c == DeliveryC && r == DeliveryR)

                                    break ;

                            }

                            lstOrder.Items.RemoveAt(i);

                        }

                    }

                }

            }

        }

 

    }

}

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

TUTORIAL 3

DRONE SIMULATION

 

 

 

In this tutorial, you will build a Drone Simulation. In this simulation, you control both vertical and horizontal thrusters to maneuver the ride to the landing pad. You will adjust the landing speed so that it is slow enough so that no accident occurs.

 

Description

You build the form in two stages, the first stage creates two option group boxes, and then the second stage uses both those group boxes as landing controls. Two control panels are placed on the left side of the form: one panel for drawing and another panel for the edge. On the right side of the form, place the two group control boxes. In the first group box, five radio buttons and a check box are added. In the second group box, two radio buttons are placed. In the below section of the form, three buttons are added. Finally, one timer control is added.

 

Figure 4.1 All controls used in Drone Simulation project

 

Then in the form, a group box is added overlap panel. Then, 11 label controls are added to the group box. After that, a progress bar is added. Under the bar, two control panels are added, one high panel and one short panel. In the second (short) panel control, two small label controls are added. Underneath, three button controls are placed. Under these three buttons, a label control is added. For each label control, set the AutoSize property to False to be resized and set (temporarily) the BorderStyle property to FixedSingle so that you can see the edges to facilitate the layout process.

 

Figure 4.2 All type of controls used in Drone Simulation project

 

Run the program (press <F5>). You can choose one pilot level by checking or unchecking the auto-pilot option. Whenever you play a game, you can restore it and restart the game, as shown in Figure 4.3.

 

Tutorial Steps

Step 1

You will now start to build this project. Open a new project in Visual C#. Once opened, it is recommended that you immediately save it with a name that you choose yourself. This will create the folders and file structure that your project needs.

 

You will build the form in two stages, the first stage creates two option group boxes, and then the second stage uses both group groups as landing controls. Place two control panels on the left side of the form: one panel for drawing and another panel for the edge. On the right side of the form, place the two group control boxes. In the first group box, place five radio buttons and a check box. In the second group box, place the two radio buttons. In the bottom-right section of the form, place three control buttons. Add one timer control. The form will look as shown in Figure 4.4.

Figure 4.3 Drone Simulation runs with auto-pilot option

 

Figure 4.4 All controls used in this project and thei locations

 

One control panel forms a frame that surrounds another panel that will display a drone landing animation. The first group box is used to select the pilot level and whether to use auto-pilot. The second group box is used to select measurement units. Two smaller button controls (one to start and pause the game and one other button to stop the game and exit the program) are used to control game operations. The larger button is used at the end of the game to see the landing result. Timer control is used to calculate landing position and speed and for animation updates.

Step 3

Even though you don't have any code yet, you can run this game. The game now is in ‘stop’ state, as shown in Figure 4.7.

 

In the “stop” state, what the user can do is choose one of the two options (Difficulty Level or Unit) or click the Start Game button or Exit . You can also decide if you want to enable Auto-Pilot . If the user chooses to start the game, two option group boxes will disappear and the landing group box ( grpControl ) will appear.

 

You will use a variable ( LevelDifficulty ) that has a range of values ​​from 1 to 5 to track the level of the selected difficulty. Add this declaration at the form level:

 

1

int levelDifficulty = 1;

 

Figure 4.7 The game now is in “stop” state

 

You initialize the Beginner level ( LevelDifficulty = 1 ) to match the radio button that was originally selected.

 

Code to set the LevelDifficulty is placed in the Click event procedure of rdoLevelDifficulty , which is the event for all radio buttons to select the difficulty level:

private void rdoLevelDifficulty_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    RadioButton ButtonClicked;

    ButtonClicked = (RadioButton)sender;

 

    switch (ButtonClicked.Text)

    {

        case "Beginner" :

            levelDifficulty = 1;

            break ;

        case "Trainee" :

            levelDifficulty = 2;

            break ;

        case "Junior" :

            levelDifficulty = 3;

            break ;

        case "Senior" :

            levelDifficulty = 4;

            break ;

        case "Advanced" :

            levelDifficulty = 5;

            break ;

    }

}

 

 

Step 4

You will calculate this program in the metrics unit. This means all positions are in meter and all speeds are in meter/sec. If the user selects an US (Britain) unit, you need to multiply all results with a value that converts meters to feet. This value will be stored in a variable named Multiplier . Add the following declaration at the form level:

 

1

double Multiplier = 1.0;

 

The multiplier for the metric unit is specified in the Click event procedure of the rdoUnitMetric radio button:

 

1

2

3

4

private void rdoUnitMetric_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    Multiplier = 1.0;

}

 

And for US (Britain) unit, Multiplier is set to the Click event procedure of rdoUnitUS :

 

1

2

3

4

private void rdoUnitUS_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    Multiplier = 3.2808;

}

 

This states that one meter is equal to 3.2808 feet.

 

Step 5

The key element in simpulation program is timer control ( timDrone ). This timer is used to update elapsed time, all values ​​calculated, and all graphic elements of the program. At this initialization stage, you only use it to update the time. Add this declaration at the form level:

 

1

double time;

 

Time is then updated in the Tick even procedure of timDrone control:

 

1

2

3

4

5

6

private void timDrone_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    time += Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

    lblTime.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , time);

    lblTime.Refresh();

}

 

You now have an Interval property of 500 milliseconds, so update is done every 0.5 second.

 

Step 6

Now, you will start writing code to start, pause, restart, and stop the game. You will also write code to exit the program. Before doing so, you need to learn what happens at each difficulty level:

  • Beginner : There is no lateral thrust control; no use of fuel.
  • Trainee : There is no vertical thrust control; no use of fuel.
  • Junior : All thrust controls are available; no use of fuel.
  • Senior , Advanced : All thrust controls are available; there is use of fuel.

 

If Auto-Pilot is on, you don't have thrust controls, so the label that says Auto-Pilot On will be made visible. Therefore, when the game starts, a number of different controls will/will not be displayed.

 

There are two game controller buttons, btnStartPause and btnExitStop . These two buttons have certain interactions. The btnStartPause control can have three possible values ​​for the Text property. If the Text property is Start Game when clicked, the game will be initialized and switched to play mode using:

  • Change the Text property of btnStartPause to Pause Game .
  • Change the Text property of btnExitStop to Stop Game .
  • Set Visible property of grpLevel and grpUnit to False .
  • Set Visible property of grpControl to True .
  • If LevelDifficulty = 1 , then: set the Text property of grpControl to Beginner ; remove the fuel lever btnThrustLeft and btnThrustRight .
  • If LevelDifficulty = 2 , then: set the Text property of grpControl to Trainee ; remove the fuel lever btnThrustDown .

Step 9

You will now start to learn a little about physics and mathematics. You will learn some equations that explain the position and speed of landing drone. As a first step, you need to define a coordinate system to do the calculation. It is assumed that graphic elements (drone, booster fire, pad, and background) are loaded in a rectangular region called Landscape .

 

 

A point in this region is specified by a Cartesian pair (x, y). In the diagram, notice the x (horizontal) coordinates increase from left to right, starting from 0 to Landscape.Width - 1 . The y (vertical) coordinates increase from top to bottom, from 0 to Landscape.Height - 1 . All measurements involve integers and in pixel units. In this program, it is assumed that one pixel is related to one meter distance.

 

Each graphic element is also contained in a rectangular structure. The drone element ( Drone ) is located in the Cartesian pair ( DroneX , DroneY ) inside the rectangular Landscape :

 

 

Drone has Drone.Width width and Drone.Height height. DroneX and DroneY are assigned initial values ​​(at Time = 0 ). Drone speed is DroneXVel ​​and DroneYVel , which are initially given a zero value.

 

After the initial values ​​for DroneX , DroneY , DroneXVel , and DroneYVel ​​are given, everything is updated (incremented or decremented) at certain times. Speed ​​is updated when thrusters are used. The speed and position are updated with each change from the starting time, which is set by timDrone control.

 

The vertical thruster only affect vertical speed, DroneYVel . This thruster produces a change in velocity called YDelta , where the equation for changing the speed in the y-direction when the thruster is applied is: DroneYVel ​​-= YDelta , with the bottom thruster applied. Vertical thruster (bottom) slow down the vertical speed, so it can be used for proper landing.

 

Horizontal thruster only affect horizontal speed, DroneXVel . This thruster produces a speed change called XDelta , where the equation for changing the speed in the x-direction when the thruster is applied is: DroneXVel ​​+= XDelta , with the left thruster applied and DroneXVel ​​-= XDelta , with the right thruster applied.

 

The left thruster slows the drone moves towards the right; the right thruster slows the drone towards the left.

 

By knowing the horizontal speed ( DroneXVel ) and vertical speed ( DroneYVel ), how do you know the position of DroneX and DroneY ? You will use the classic formula: Distance = Speed ​​x TravelTime .

 

This equation is derived from a branch of mathematics known as Calculus. This calculation is done every time the timer updates it (in the Tick event of the timDrone ). Suppose that T is the interval of the timer control in seconds: T = timDrone.Interval / 1000, then the X and Y positions of the drone are updated each time cycle using: DroneX += DroneXVel * T and DroneY += DroneYVel * T .

 

You certainly know that DroneXVel * T is the horizontal distance traveled by drone at one time cycle and DroneYVel * T is the horizontal distance traveled by drone at one time cycle

 

Vertical speed ( DroneYVel ) also changes at each time cycle. Gravity tends to increase when the drone approaches the surface. If the speed of gravity is Gravity, in T second, the speed increases according to: DroneYVel ​​+ = Gravity * T .

 

You can also change the horizontal speed ( DroneXVel ) at each time cycle. If you apply horizontal thruster in one direction, the drone will continue in the direction of that driving thrust in the other direction applied. To counter this effect, if the drone moves horizontally, you can use the term "drag" to slow it down, even without a thruster. If the dragging constant is Drag , the resulting speed correction is DroneXVel​ ​-= Drag , if DroneXVel > 0 , and DroneXVel ​​+ = Drag , if DroneXVel ​​<0 .

 

This concludes the updating equations for the position and speed of the drone. You then modify the project to include these equations. Add four form level variables to calculate position and speed:

 

1

2

double DroneX, DroneY;

double DroneXVel, DroneYVel;

private void timDrone_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    time += Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

    lblTime.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , time);

    lblTime.Refresh();

 

    DroneX += DroneXVel * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval)/1000;

    DroneY += DroneYVel * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

    UpdateStatus();

 

    // Horizontal dragging

    if (DroneXVel > 0)

        DroneXVel -= Drag;

    else if (DroneXVel < 0)

        DroneXVel += Drag;

 

    // Graivity

    DroneYVel += Gravity * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

}

 

Additionally, return to the Click event from btnStartPause and add this line of code after initializing the speed and position of the drone: UpdateStatus() . This initializes the displays correctly.

Step 15

As noted, the displayed values ​​do not answer the question how far is the drone from the landing pad. You are about to add a graphic element, Pad . The Pad element (a rectangular structure) is placed at a location ( Pad X, PadY ), with the width of the Pad.Width and height of the Pad.Height :

 

 

In this sketch, you add two distances. Altitude determines how far the drone is above the landing pad. This is the distance of the drone to the center of the runway: Altitude = (Landscape.Height - Pad.Height / 2) - (DroneY + Drone.Height) . Notice Altitude decreases when drone goes down ( DroneY increases). Altitude represents the height above the pad, which approaches zero when the drone gets closer to the runway.

 

Figure 4.10 Landscape image

 

Another distance, Lateral , sets the horizontal distance of the drone to the runway (pad). This is the middle distance of the drone to the center of the pad: Lateral = (DroneX + Drone.Width) - (PadX + Pad.Width) .

 

Note that Lateral is positive if the drone is on the right side of the pad, negative if it is on the left of the pad. Lateral is zero if the drone is directly above the pad.

 

You can add these equations to the program to get the value ​​of Altitude and Lateral , but one problem remains. You do not know the size of each image used. You will solve this now. You will use five images in the program: Landscape, Drone, Pad, HThrust, and VThrust. You will see each of these images.

Figure 4.11 Drone image

Figure 4.12 Pad image

private void UpdateStatus()

{

    Altitude = (Landscape.Height - Pad.Height / 2) –

        (DroneY + Drone.Height);

    Lateral = (DroneX + Drone.Width / 2) - (PadX + Pad.Width / 2);

 

    if (Altitude > 0)

        lblVPosition.Text = String.Format( "{0:f0}" ,

            Altitude * Multiplier);

    else

        lblVPosition.Text = "0" ;

    if (Math.Abs(Lateral) < 1)

        lblHPosition.Text = "Above" ;

    else

        lblHPosition.Text = String.Format( "{0:f0}" ,

            Lateral * Multiplier);

 

    lblVVel.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , -DroneYVel * Multiplier);

    lblHVel.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , DroneXVel * Multiplier);

 

    lblVVel.Refresh();

   lblHVel.Refresh();

   lblVPosition.Refresh();

   lblHPosition.Refresh();

}

 

You now have equations for calculating Altitude and Lateral . For vertical position labels, DroneY is replaced by Altitude (by limiting the value to zero). On the horizontal speed label, a negative sign is added to indicate a negative speed that indicates a reduced altitude. For horizontal position, DroneX is replaced by Lateral .

private void timDrone_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    time += Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

    lblTime.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , time);

    lblTime.Refresh();

 

    DroneX += DroneXVel * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval)/1000;

    DroneY += DroneYVel * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

    UpdateStatus();

 

    // Checks landing

    if (Altitude <= 0)

    {

        timDrone.Enabled = false ;

        btnThrustLeft.Visible = false ;

        btnThrustRight.Visible = false ;

        btnThrustDown.Visible = false ;

 

        if (chkAutoPilot.Checked)

            lblMessage.Text = "Auto-Pilot " ;

        else

        {

            lblMessage.Text = "You " ;

            lblMessage.Visible = true ;

        }

 

        // Crash?

        if (DroneYVel > VelLandingSafe)

        {

            lblMessage.Text += "Crash!" ;

        }

        else

        {

            lblMessage.Text += "Land Safely" ;

        }

 

        // Makes btnFinish visible

        btnStartPause.Visible = false ;

        btnExitStop.Visible = false ;

        btnFinish.Visible = true ;

        return ;

    }

 

    // Horizontal dragging

    if (DroneXVel > 0)

        DroneXVel -= Drag;

    else if (DroneXVel < 0)

        DroneXVel += Drag;

 

    // Graivity

    DroneYVel += Gravity * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

}

 

In this code, after Altitude has reached zero, timDrone will be disabled, thruster buttons will be removed and certain landing message will be displayed based on vertical speed (and based on whether auto-pilot is enabled or not).

Step 23

Although no penalty is given if the landing fails, you need to know during the flight how close the drone is to the pad. One indication is the position value displayed on the label control. Graphic indicator will be very helpful. The first graphic indicator to be used are the green ( lblDrone ) and red ( lblPad ) labels on the panel ( pnlGuide ) under the trajectory panel.

 

The green square represents the horizontal position of the drone, while the red square represents the landing pad. The midpoint of each label control in the guide will coincide with the middle of the drone image and the pad image in the landscape panel. Or, with a simple calculation of the Left propertiy, you get:

 

lblDrone.Left = (DroneX + Drone.Width / 2) * (pnlGuide.Width / Landscape.Width) - lblDrone.Width / 2 and lblPad.Left = (PadX + Pad.Width / 2) * (pnlGuide.Width / Landscape.Width) - lblPad.Width / 2.

 

Add these two equations to the end of the UpdateStatus procedure.

private void UpdateStatus()

{

    Altitude = (Landscape.Height - Pad.Height / 2) –

        (DroneY + Drone.Height);

    Lateral = (DroneX + Drone.Width / 2) - (PadX + Pad.Width / 2);

 

    if (Altitude > 0)

        lblVPosition.Text = String.Format( "{0:f0}" ,

            Altitude * Multiplier);

    else

        lblVPosition.Text = "0" ;

    if (Math.Abs(Lateral) < 1)

        lblHPosition.Text = "Above" ;

    else

        lblHPosition.Text = String.Format( "{0:f0}" ,

            Lateral * Multiplier);

 

    lblVVel.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , -DroneYVel * Multiplier);

    lblHVel.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , DroneXVel * Multiplier);

 

    lblVVel.Refresh();

    lblHVel.Refresh();

    lblVPosition.Refresh();

    lblHPosition.Refresh();

 

    lblDrone.Left = Convert.ToInt32((DroneX + Drone.Width / 2) *

        pnlGuide.Width / Landscape.Width - lblDrone.Width / 2);

    lblPad.Left = Convert.ToInt32((PadX + Pad.Width / 2) *

        pnlGuide.Width / Landscape.Width - lblPad.Width / 2);

}

 

Save and run the project. Green and red squares will indicate the horizontal location of the lander against the pad.

private void timDrone_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    time += Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

    lblTime.Text = String.Format( "{0:f1}" , time);

    lblTime.Refresh();

 

    DroneX += DroneXVel * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval)/1000;

    DroneY += DroneYVel * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

    UpdateStatus();

 

    // Checks landing

    if (Altitude <= 0)

    {

        timDrone.Enabled = false ;

        btnThrustLeft.Visible = false ;

        btnThrustRight.Visible = false ;

        btnThrustDown.Visible = false ;

 

        if (chkAutoPilot.Checked)

            lblMessage.Text = "Auto-Pilot " ;

        else

        {

            lblMessage.Text = "You " ;

            lblMessage.Visible = true ;

        }

 

        // Crash?

        if (DroneYVel > VelLandingSafe)

        {

            SoundCrashLanding.PlaySync();

            lblMessage.Text += "Crash!" ;

        }

        else

        {

            SoundSafeLanding.PlaySync();

            lblMessage.Text += "Land Safely" ;

        }

 

        // Makes btnFinish visible

        btnStartPause.Visible = false ;

        btnExitStop.Visible = false ;

        btnFinish.Visible = true ;

        return ;

    }

 

    // Horizontal dragging

    if (DroneXVel > 0)

        DroneXVel -= Drag;

    else if (DroneXVel < 0)

        DroneXVel += Drag;

 

    // Graivity

    DroneYVel += Gravity * Convert.ToDouble(timDrone.Interval) / 1000;

}
